parsed.explanation: The combined operative regime is dominated by national measures that reach any trans visitor. The passport sex-marker restriction is in force after the November 2025 Supreme Court ruling, and passports have been confiscated or blocked, leaving some travellers stranded. Entry refusal under the case-note cable is documented, with a lifetime fraud-ineligibility route. Immigration custody shows documented beatings and severe sexual abuse of trans men, and federal corrections adopted conversion-style policies. The national legislature's bathroom restriction applies locally, with arrests recorded at the national legislature building. Local protections (anti-discrimination, a seat-level low-risk placement) operate but are overridable by the national legislature, and the durability caveat weakens them. Scope of the facilities ban and local custody, hate-crime and document practice are unsourced.

entry_documents.exposure: Passports refused or confiscated; new applications issued only as M or F; entry refusal and lifetime-ineligibility route under a fraud ground for suspected misrepresentation; 'X' markers no longer issued for new applications.
entry_documents.protection: Existing X-marker passports valid to expiry; litigation pending; no documented operative relief for travellers.
entry_documents.interaction: Universal national document rule applies to every crossing and every passport check; local protections do not reach border or passport decisions.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: Immigration custody: documented forced labour, beatings, solitary confinement and severe sexual abuse of trans men. National prisons adopted conversion-style policies (hair cutting, hormone removal) and stopped reporting trans prisoner counts.
investigation_detention_custody.protection: Not documented as operative for trans detainees; advocacy litigation noted but unresolved.
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: Detention risk follows from document discrepancy at entry and carries federal custody rules, so the harshest national custody regime governs the visitor's experience.

federal_state_facilities.exposure: National legislature's facilities restriction applies in this jurisdiction; scope (which buildings, whether visitors are reached) is not specified. Arrests at the national legislature building on 5 December 2024 for protesting it.
federal_state_facilities.protection: No local bathroom ban of its own; local law is protective but can be overridden by national action and is not treated as settled.
federal_state_facilities.interaction: Local protective law is subordinate to the national facilities restriction; the more restrictive operative rule governs use of public facilities.

care_services.exposure: National subpoenas of hospital records for patients under 19; federal youth crisis-line services shut; proposed rule to bar public insurance for under-18 care; reduced care access for minors.
care_services.protection: Adult care access not documented as restricted locally; no documented operative local care protection beyond general law.
care_services.interaction: Care exposure is national; a visitor with a minor faces record-disclosure exposure that local law does not offset.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: National counterterrorism strategy names 'radically pro-transgender' groups as a neutralisation priority; December 2025 reward system references 'radical gender ideology'; executive order directs prosecution of teachers facilitating social transition.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.protection: Counterterrorism statement says powers will not target mere disagreement; several orders enjoined.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: Official framing at national level is hostile; local institutions cannot offset it, and visitors may be scrutinised through national security channels.

minors_guardians.exposure: Minor-directed executive orders; records subpoenas for under-19 patients; potential criminal exposure for those assisting a minor's social transition; minors' care restricted in 27 state/provinces.
minors_guardians.protection: Not documented as operative for travelling minors locally.
minors_guardians.interaction: A travelling guardian of a trans minor faces both national records and enforcement exposure that local protections do not reach.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: Single documented trans-specific violence pattern not reported locally; federal hate statute exists but 37 state/provinces lacked gender-identity bias statutes (2019). Bias against sexual orientation is the larger share of single-bias hate incidents.
street_violence_police_response.protection: National gender-identity hate-crime statute; local anti-discrimination protection for gender identity documented; local protective law stated as in force.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: Recourse exists nationally and locally but street-level violence data are not disaggregated for trans visitors.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: Local document practice, local custody conditions, local police practice, and enforcement scope of the national facilities ban are not sourced. Court challenges unresolved; the July 2026 low-risk placement's method is unverifiable.
remedies_unknowns.protection: Local protective law and national marriage recognition operate, though overridable; legal-aid FAQ exists.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: The visitor's exposure at border and in federal custody is not offset by local protections; unknowns are treated as open questions, not safety.

anchor_checks.comparison: Similar in entry-document exclusion: a register-based refusal regime with refusals consistent for visible trans travellers. This case documents national passport blocking and stranding and a lifetime-ineligibility route, which is comparable. It is lower in severity since no appeal-denial record is documented, but it adds documented custody abuse.

Closest in custody severity: birth-sex or cross-dressing enforcement in custody with assaults and solitary confinement. Here immigration custody abuse is documented with sexual abuse and a national prison conversion-style regime, which is comparable. It sits slightly above because local protective law operates in the division, but it lacks documented birth-sex housing and capital exposure.

Similar in universal exposure through document verification and registration. This case lacks documented registration databases for visitors, but it adds active national prosecution and custody harms, so it sits slightly below.

Comparable in entry screening and document-driven denial with largely administrative penalties. This case is lower because it documents custody abuse and national care and records exposure, while the 0.55-B case has more recourse and no documented custodial harm.

parsed.synthesis: The documented national regime (passport sex-marker restriction, refusal and fraud-ineligibility routes, and immigration custody abuse) applies to every visitor and is the operative exposure. Local protections, including a low-risk seat-level placement and a local anti-discrimination statute, are real but are subordinate to the national legislature's facilities restriction and can be overridden. The local facilities ban has an unspecified scope and documented arrests of protesters, not visitors. Lack of recorded local violence is not counted as safety. The rating sits in the high-to-elevated range, below the Reduced Risk line, because documented custody harm and universal document exposure outweigh the local protections.
